name: Tyrrell P34
hook: Four of its six wheels sit at the front, ten inches tall, and it is still the only six-wheeled car ever to win a Formula 1 Grand Prix.
story: The whole car rests on a tyre nobody else ran. Derek Gardner worked out that four small front wheels, tucked inside the bodywork, would lift the nose less than two big ones. They would also put more rubber on the road and leave more room for brakes. Goodyear agreed to make them: ten inches tall, built for one team. When the cover came off at a hotel near Heathrow in September 1975, hoops underneath had kept the silhouette looking ordinary. Even the drivers had not been told. At Anderstorp in June 1976 it all came good. Jody Scheckter led Patrick Depailler home, first and second, the only Grand Prix a six-wheeler has ever won. Then the trouble arrived quietly. Goodyear kept improving the big tyres that every other team used, and left the little ones where they were. Gardner called that development non-existent. The car grew slower without changing a bolt. By 1978 Tyrrell was back on four wheels.
description: The Tyrrell P34 was a Formula 1 car designed by Derek Gardner for Ken Tyrrell's team. It raced through 1976 and 1977 on four small front wheels and two ordinary rear ones, around an aluminium monocoque with a Ford-Cosworth DFV V8 behind the driver. Portholes were cut in the cockpit sides so the driver could watch the front tyres wear. Seven were built. Its best year was 1976, when Tyrrell finished third in the constructors' championship.
